content:
sam-sales: Heads up — BetaCorp POC reporting missing trace_ids in Splunk after we enabled direct HEC export. Also saw a couple of 429 spikes during their load tests. Can we triage?

darya-se: Which exporter/settings are they using? HEC needs proper content-type and sometimes rejects dot-keys. Any sample payloads?

sam-sales: they attached a raw post from the forwarder:```
POST /services/collector/event HTTP/1.1
Host: splunk.example.com
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Encoding: gzip
Authorization: Splunk <token>

<gzipped-payload>
```
When we decompress, payload looks like:```json
{"time":1700000000,"event":{"request_id":"r-555","trace":{"id":"tr-xyz","span":"s2"},"msg":"ok"}}
```
but Splunk search shows event without trace or trace.id.

jordan-sre: two hypotheses: 1) HEC is configured with a strict sourcetype that drops nested objects, 2) Flattening or a pre-HEC transform turned trace.id into a dotted key which their ingest pipeline strips. Also gzip+chunking shouldn't drop fields but some proxies unwrap badly.

sam-sales: customer said their infra team saw our requests occasionally return 429 from our endpoint and their forwarder retried, creating bursts. They reduced forwarder concurrency and saw fewer 429s.

darya-se: actionable items: ask for a raw decompressed single-event JSON as captured right before HEC; ask for their HEC props/transforms. Meanwhile we can add a mapping option on our side to rename nested keys to safe flat names (trace_id).

sam-sales: customer pasted this minimal example they claim appears in our Console:```
{ "request_id": "r-555", "trace": { "id": "tr-xyz", "span": "s2" }, "status": "ok" }
```
And the event they see in Splunk:```
{ "request_id": "r-555", "trace.id": "tr-xyz" }
```
So trace became a single dotted key and Splunk didn't index it into their trace field.

jordan-sre: that fits. Quick fixes: 1) advise them to disable dot-key stripping in HEC, 2) add a transform mapping from "trace.id" -> "trace_id", or 3) stop flattening on forwarder. Which do they prefer?

sam-sales: their security team prefers not to change Splunk props. They asked if we can do a transform on our exporter for the POC.

darya-se: we can implement a per-POC transform that rewrites dot-keys to underscored keys. I'll push a canary that runs only for BetaCorp. Also will add 429-aware backoff and a per-tenant backpressure metric available in Console.

opsbot: Canary deploy initiated: export-transform-beta-2026-03-21 @eng-runtime (build 4180)

leo-support: for a quick workaround, share this mapping snippet with their forwarding team they can drop in their forwarder config:```json
{"field_mappings": [{"from":"trace.id","to":"trace_id"},{"from":"trace.span","to":"span_id"}]}
```

sam-sales: passed mapping; customer applied it and confirmed trace_id appears in Splunk immediately. They still saw 2 429s during a 10k qps spike but reduced after we suggested lowering concurrency and enabling retries.

jordan-sre: once canary is live we'll instrument a per-tenant 429 counter and last-5-samples to trace spikes. Also add a note to POC playbook: prefer content-type application/json without unnecessary flattening, and recommend batch_size 10-20 for HEC in high-burst setups.

darya-se: canary deployed. opsbot: Deploy success 90% traffic to canary, 2 healthy instances.

opsbot: Metrics emitted: beta-poc.429_count=3, beta-poc.last_429_ts=1700000005

leo-support: follow-ups: 1) prod-ify dot-key -> underscore transform (+docs), 2) add Splunk HEC sample configs to POC repo, 3) expose per-tenant 429 alerts in Console.

sam-sales: BetaCorp thanks the team — they said the quick mapping + our config guidance saved the demo. Closing this thread unless they reopen. :party:
